solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mental suffering can, leading to great piece of art

parts.note: pain can be mental anguish as well as physical hurt
a tin is a can

indicators.note: the leading letter of the word great is the one taken

explanation.surface: Someone's anguish over a can that inspires a great artwork, Warhol-style.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting is a single work of art on canvas or board.

clue.text: A holiday offers naught for a hobbyist's interest

indicators.note: naught stands in place of the letter a, so one swaps for the other

parts.note: a vacation is a holiday
the letter a
naught is zero, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A holiday gives nothing to someone whose hobby is their real interest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offers' is only a link; 'for' signals the swap of a letter A for zero. The definition is a side pursuit, not a calling.
explanation.definitionFit: An avocation is a pursuit followed for pleasure beside one's regular work.

clue.text: Almost needs to fasten loose garment

parts.note: nigh means nearly or almost
to tie is to fasten

explanation.surface: A loose garment almost needs fastening to stay on.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightdress is a loose gown worn in bed.

clue.text: Fabulous flower died taken from wild orchid

indicators.note: wild signals the remaining letters running riot into a new order
the letter for died is removed from the word orchid

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for died, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A fabulous bloom that died after being taken from a wild orchid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is something that flows: the fluid in the veins of the Greek gods, hence 'fabulous', from fable.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this ethereal fluid flowed in the gods' veins in place of blood.

clue.text: Fish in newspaper served up

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper

explanation.surface: Fish served up wrapped in newspaper, like chips.
explanation.definitionFit: The garfish is a long slender fish with a needle-like beak.

clue.text: Eccentricities of queen annoy society

parts.note: to irk is to annoy

explanation.surface: A queen's eccentricities annoy polite society.
explanation.definitionFit: Quirks are peculiar habits or oddities of behaviour.

clue.text: What can draw one in like our easy cryptic with a bit of grit?

parts.note: The Times publishes a Quick Cryptic, its easier daily puzzle
sand is fine grit

explanation.surface: Is our gentler puzzle, with a dash of grit, what lures solvers in?
explanation.walkthrough: The Times runs a beginner-friendly Quick Cryptic alongside this puzzle, which supplies the first part.
explanation.definitionFit: Wet loose sand sucks in anything that steps onto it.

clue.text: Indium-copper conductor is a source of difficulty

parts.note: In is the chemical symbol for indium
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a bus or busbar is an electrical conductor

explanation.surface: An indium-copper conductor proves troublesome to an electrical engineer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conductor' looks like a person on a bus, but here it is the bus itself, an electrical busbar.
explanation.definitionFit: An incubus is a nightmare demon, so figuratively an oppressive burden or worry.

clue.text: Dull colour is something motorists want to go, some say?

indicators.note: some say signals that the words are pronounced in a certain accent

parts.note: a car key is what a driver needs to get going

explanation.surface: A dull colour that drivers want to go, as some put it.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone works in a non-rhotic accent, where the R of car is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: This drab brownish-yellow is the colour of army uniforms.

clue.text: Number fifty-six is lost from your present mission?

indicators.note: the Roman number is taken out of the activity word

parts.note: what the reader is doing right now is working out the crossword
LVI is 56 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A mysterious task where a number is mislaid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Your present mission' is the act of SOLVING this crossword.
explanation.definitionFit: A number is a piece of music performed, such as a tune.

clue.text: Shore creature caught with right bait swimming near Channel island

indicators.note: near puts the island beside the rearranged letters

parts.note: Herm is one of the small Channel Islands, near Guernsey

indicators.note: swimming suggests letters moving about loosely

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A shore creature is caught with the right bait off a Channel island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimming' rearranges C, R and BAIT into ITCRAB.
explanation.definitionFit: This crustacean lives on beaches and in rock pools, sheltering in empty shells.

clue.text: Amphibian jet car goes haywire in fluid tank

indicators.note: in places the first scrambled group within the second
fluid means not fixed in form, so these letters move too
something going haywire is out of control, so the letters scramble

explanation.surface: A jet car runs amok in a tank of liquid, absurdly turning amphibious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fluid' seems to describe what fills the tank but is a second anagram signal; 'goes haywire' scrambles the car, and 'in' nests one jumble in the other.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a European toad, so an amphibian.

clue.text: Transparency shown by excellent gallery

parts.note: ace means excellent
the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: A transparency displayed in a top-class gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a group of major British art galleries.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetate film was used for overhead-projector transparencies.

clue.text: Officer briefly seen in naval prison

definitions.meaning: a short form of brigadier, an army officer

explanation.surface: An officer briefly spotted in a ship's jail.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an abbreviated army rank and the cells on a warship, especially in American usage.

clue.text: Professor of knowledge we care about is accepted

indicators.note: accepted means taken in, so the word is goes inside
about here means around in a jumble, so those letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An academic says they care about what is accepted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' rearranges WE CARE to WEACRE; 'accepted' takes IS inside after W. 'Professor' means one who professes, not an academic.
explanation.definitionFit: A smart alec claims to know everything, professing wisdom they lack.

clue.text: Signs of age shown by quarrels over payment in court

indicators.note: in places these words inside the court abbreviation
in a down clue, over puts the first word above the second

parts.note: rows are quarrels
a fee is a payment

explanation.surface: Signs of ageing appear after courtroom quarrels over fees.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the fine wrinkles at the outer corners of the eyes that come with age.

clue.text: Weigh up topless girls son's chasing

indicators.note: chasing means following behind
topless means the first letter comes off

parts.note: lasses are girls
S is the abbreviation for son, with 's as is

explanation.surface: A son eyes up topless girls, judging them.
explanation.definitionFit: To assess is to evaluate or judge.

clue.text: A pact goes wrong: this one takes the blame

indicators.note: going wrong means going awry, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: When an agreement collapses, someone always carries the can.
explanation.definitionFit: A fall guy is blamed for the faults of others.

clue.text: Blue diamonds one's kept in home are stolen?

indicators.note: kept in means held inside

parts.note: in means at home
things that go have vanished, as stolen goods do
D is the abbreviation for the suit of diamonds
I is one, as a Roman numeral; one's means one is

explanation.surface: Blue diamonds kept at home are stolen.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo is a deep violet-blue.

clue.text: Insult art endlessly? That's narrow-minded

indicators.note: endlessly removes the final letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: Endlessly insulting art reveals a closed mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Insular people are cut off from outside ideas, like an island.

clue.text: A little land's needing two gates bolted

indicators.note: needing joins the gates to the running away word

parts.note: AND and OR are two logic gates in electronics
ran means bolted, ran off

explanation.surface: A small country needs two gates shut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolted' looks like locked, but means RAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Andorra is a tiny Pyrenean principality, so this adjective means belonging to it.

clue.text: Italian dish is extreme, eaten by half of Rome

indicators.note: eaten by means held within
half of takes the first two of four letters

parts.note: OTT is over the top, extreme

explanation.surface: An Italian dish so extreme that half of Rome eats it.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is a creamy Italian rice dish.

clue.text: What bookie offers ultimately to defraud bad betters

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of each word

explanation.surface: A crooked bookmaker's prices are set to cheat poor gamblers.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookmaker sets prices that determine the payout on a bet.

clue.text: Comic sent up Liberal peer

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a lord is a peer

explanation.surface: A comedian mocks a Liberal member of the Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent up' looks like mocking, but means written upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Droll means amusing in a dry way.

clue.text: How to choreograph a ballet being staged?

definitions.meaning: a dance is planned one movement at a time
staged means done in stages, gradually

explanation.surface: How dance is arranged for a production.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means gradually, one stage at a time, and literally describes dance moves.

clue.text: Steep wave on river is a problem for some ships?

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the first above the second

parts.note: a bore is a tidal wave surging up a river

explanation.surface: A steep wave on a river troubles certain ships.
explanation.definitionFit: A shipworm drills into the timbers of wooden ships.

clue.text: One saving object again to look quickly over

parts.note: goal means object or aim

indicators.note: over means turned over, read backwards

parts.note: re- means again
to peek is to look quickly

explanation.surface: Someone saving an object to peek at again.
explanation.definitionFit: A keeper's job in football is to make saves.

clue.text: Work steadily at college once, avoiding second

indicators.note: avoiding second means the second letter of the old college word is dropped

parts.note: polys, or polytechnics, were colleges in Britain until 1992

explanation.surface: Studying steadily at an old college, missing a second.
explanation.definitionFit: To ply a trade is to work at it diligently.

clue.text: Former city politician has a change of heart

indicators.note: the central letters swap places

parts.note: a Tory is a British Conservative

explanation.surface: A politician changes their mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Troy was the ancient city of the Trojan War.

clue.text: Worry about large old piece of broccoli

indicators.note: about in its sense of around, so the worry word wraps round the other letters

parts.note: to fret is to worry

explanation.surface: Fretting about a big old piece of broccoli.
explanation.definitionFit: A floret is a small flowering head on broccoli.

clue.text: Lad found carrying weapon in Norfolk town

indicators.note: carrying means holding inside

parts.note: youth means a lad
an arm is a weapon

explanation.surface: A boy found carrying a gun in a Norfolk town.
explanation.definitionFit: Great Yarmouth is a resort on the Norfolk coast.
